title: 1998 HMMT February Algebra Problem 4
statement: Given that \(r\) and \(s\) are relatively prime positive integers such that \(\frac{r}{s}=\frac{2(\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{10})}{5(\sqrt{3+\sqrt{5}})}\), find \(r\) and \(s\).

solutions.text: Squaring both sides of the given equation yields \(\frac{r^{2}}{s^{2}}=\frac{4(12+4 \sqrt{5})}{25(3+\sqrt{5})}=\frac{16(3+\sqrt{5})}{25(3+\sqrt{5})}=\frac{16}{25}\). Because \(r\) and \(s\) are positive and relatively prime, then by inspection, \(r=4\) and \(s=5\).
